title: How can I manage firmware updates and troubleshoot issues for Genea-managed controllers?
text:
## Managing Firmware Updates and Troubleshooting for Genea-Managed Controllers
Genea provides a robust system for managing controllers, including firmware updates and troubleshooting. This article outlines the key processes and considerations for managing firmware updates, syncing, and resolving common issues.
Overview of Firmware Updates
Firmware updates for Genea-managed controllers are not automatic. They require user initiation or a request to Genea for backend processing. Here are the key points to know:
- User-Initiated Updates: Users can perform firmware updates locally using the firmware file provided by Mercury. Access the controller’s web interface by entering its IP address in a web browser and logging in with the provided credentials. To enable authentication, set DIP switch 1 on the controller to the ON position.
- Backend Updates: Alternatively, users can request Genea to push the update from the backend.
Performing Updates: User vs. Support Roles
- End User Capabilities: End users can update firmware if they have the necessary firmware file from Mercury. This provides flexibility for users who prefer to manage updates independently.
- Support Assistance: For users who prefer not to perform updates themselves, Genea can handle the process upon request.
Troubleshooting Update Issues
- Interrupted Updates: Interrupting a firmware update will not brick the controller, providing reassurance during the update process.
- Older Firmware Versions: Stable older versions (e.g., 2.3, 2.4) do not require updates unless new features in the latest version are specifically desired.
Syncing and Data Retention
Controllers do not perform full syncs automatically. By default, only incremental updates are synced. If a controller loses power and its backup battery is removed, stored data may be erased. In such cases:
1. The controller may come online but lack configuration.
2. A manual full sync is required to restore the panel’s information.
If another controller retains power and data, it can reconnect and function without needing a full sync.
FAQs on Controller Management
When can a firmware update be performed?
Firmware updates can only be performed after the hardware is installed. Before installation, communication protocols (e.g., OSDP) can be changed, but the firmware update itself requires the hardware to be in place.
How do I log in to the controller to update firmware?
Access the controller’s web interface by entering its IP address in a web browser. Use the provided credentials to log in. To enable authentication, set DIP switch 1 on the controller to the ON position.
Can an interrupted firmware update damage the controller?
No, interrupting a firmware update will not brick the controller.
Do I need to update older firmware versions?
No, older stable versions do not require updates unless you want the latest features.
Related Topics
- Controller Connectivity and Reset Procedures
- Mercury Controller and Wireless Lock Configuration

title: How does controller connectivity affect door operations and troubleshooting?
text:
## How Does Controller Connectivity Affect Door Operations and Troubleshooting?
Understanding how controller connectivity impacts door operations is crucial for effectively managing and troubleshooting access control systems. This article provides an overview of controller functionality, common connectivity issues, and troubleshooting steps to resolve problems related to disabled doors.
Overview of Controller Functionality
Controllers play a vital role in managing door operations within the Genea system. They store access data locally, ensuring that doors can operate even during network outages. As long as the controller has power and access data, it will continue to enforce the configured settings. However, certain functionalities, such as remote locking or unlocking, require an active network connection.
Common Connectivity Issues
1. Network Loss: If the internet connection is disabled, the controller will still operate locally, but remote commands will not function. Disabling the internet does not cut power to the lock or release it, as there is no programming option to remove power via a network outage.
2. Controller Offline: When a controller is offline, doors may appear disabled in the Genea app, and remote commands such as locking or unlocking will fail. This is because the controller is unable to communicate with the system to execute these commands.
Troubleshooting Steps for Disabled Doors
If you encounter issues with a disabled door or failed remote commands, follow these steps:
1. Verify Controller Connectivity: Check whether the controller is online and connected to the network. This is the most common cause of remote command failures.
2. Ensure Power Supply: Confirm that the controller has power. Without power, the controller cannot enforce access settings or operate the door.
3. Check Local Settings: If the controller is offline but powered, ensure that the local settings are correctly configured to allow door operations.
FAQs on Controller and Door Operations
Why doesn’t disabling the internet unlock the door?
Disabling the internet does not affect the controller’s ability to operate the door locally. The controller stores access data and continues to enforce settings as long as it has power. There is no programming option to release the lock via a network outage.
Why can’t I remotely control a door that appears disabled in the app?
If a door is disabled and remote commands fail, it is likely that the controller is offline. Verify the controller’s connectivity to restore remote functionality.
___________________________________________________________
By understanding the role of controller connectivity and following these troubleshooting steps, you can effectively manage and resolve issues related to door operations in the Genea system.

title: How can I troubleshoot email issues during user onboarding in Genea?
text:
## How can I troubleshoot email issues during user onboarding in Genea?
Email communication plays a crucial role in the user onboarding process in Genea. This article provides an overview of common email-related issues, their causes, and steps to resolve them.
Overview of Email Communication in User Onboarding
Genea uses email to facilitate user onboarding. Depending on the user's role and actions taken during the setup process, emails may or may not be sent. Here are the key points:
- Admin Users: Admin users receive invitation emails to access the portal. If the email is not received, it could be due to spam filters or IT restrictions.
- Standard Users: Standard users do not receive email links unless they are issued a mobile credential or set as an admin. This is because standard users do not have portal access.
- Newly Added Tenant Users: These users receive an activation link via email, which is valid for 24 hours.
Troubleshooting Steps for Email Delivery Issues
If an email is not received, follow these steps to resolve the issue:
1. Check Spam or Junk Folders: Ask the recipient to look for the email in their spam or junk folder.
2. Whitelist the Email Domain: Ensure that the email domain used by Genea is not blocked by the recipient's IT department. This can often resolve delivery issues.
Role-Specific Email Behaviors
- Admin Users: Admins are the primary recipients of invitation emails. Ensure their email address is correctly entered during the setup process.
- Standard Users: These users will not receive emails unless specific actions, such as issuing a mobile credential, are taken.
- Tenant Users: Activation emails are sent automatically but are time-sensitive, with a 24-hour validity period.
Time-Sensitive Actions
Activation links sent to newly added tenant users are valid for 24 hours. Ensure that the recipient acts promptly to avoid the need for re-sending the link.
Additional Resources
For further assistance, contact Genea Support or consult the Genea Help Center for more detailed troubleshooting guides.

title: How to manage doors in the Genea system, including adding, configuring, and naming them?
text:
## How to Manage Doors in the Genea System, Including Adding, Configuring, and Naming Them
Managing doors in the Genea system involves adding new doors, configuring their associated readers, and ensuring proper naming conventions. This guide provides step-by-step instructions to help you effectively manage doors in the system.
Overview of Door Management in Genea
The Genea system allows administrators to manage doors and their associated readers efficiently. Proper configuration and naming are essential for maintaining an organized and functional access control system.
Adding and Configuring Doors
To add and configure a door in the Genea system, follow these steps:
1. Access the Hardware Section: - Navigate to the Genea admin dashboard. - Go to Hardware → Doors.
2. Add a New Door: - Click on the option to add a new door. - Enter a name and description for the door.
3. Attach a Reader: - Select the reader model number, reader type, controller, and the reader port. - If the controller shows Wiegand, you can change the communication protocol as needed. Otherwise, proceed with OSDP at 9600 baud if configured that way on your hardware.
4. Save the Configuration: - Complete the remaining details and click Save to add the reader.
5. Adjust Communication Protocol (if needed): - Open the interface panel detailed page. - Scroll to the reader section and click the name of the reader port you want to update. - Adjust the protocol as required.
These steps ensure that the door and its associated reader are properly configured in the Genea system.
Editing Door Names
To edit the name of an existing door:
1. Navigate to the Hardware section.
2. Select the door you want to rename.
3. Click Edit in the top-right corner.
4. Update the name and click Save.
This process allows you to keep door names accurate and up-to-date.
Best Practices for Naming and Configuration
- Use Descriptive Names: Name doors based on their location or function, such as "Lobby Exit" or "Main Entrance." This helps in identifying doors easily within the system.
- Avoid Unintended Changes: Ensure that controller names and configurations are not altered unintentionally during the setup process.
- Follow Site Requirements: Align door names and configurations with site-specific requirements to maintain consistency and compliance.
For example, when adding a lobby exit reader, configure the panel and port correctly and name the door accordingly in the system.
Conclusion
By following these guidelines, you can efficiently manage doors in the Genea system, ensuring proper configuration and naming conventions. This not only enhances system organization but also improves overall access control management.

title: How do manual and momentary unlocks affect door schedules, and how can schedules be maintained?
text:
## How do manual and momentary unlocks affect door schedules, and how can schedules be maintained?
Managing door schedules effectively is crucial for maintaining security and operational efficiency. This article explains the differences between manual and momentary unlocks, their impact on door schedules, and best practices for ensuring schedules are followed.
Overview of Door Unlock Scheduling
Door unlock schedules are predefined configurations that determine when doors should automatically lock or unlock. These schedules are essential for ensuring that access is granted or restricted at appropriate times without manual intervention.
Differences Between Manual and Momentary Unlocks
- Momentary Unlock: A momentary unlock temporarily unlocks the door for a short period. Once the momentary unlock period ends, the door reverts to its scheduled behavior. This ensures that the schedule remains intact and continues to function as configured.
- Manual Unlock: A manual unlock overrides the schedule entirely, leaving the door unlocked until it is manually locked again. This action disrupts the schedule and requires additional steps to restore the schedule's functionality.
Ensuring Schedule Compliance After Manual Unlocks
If a door has been manually unlocked, you can take steps to ensure it follows its schedule again:
1. Create an I/O Rule: Set up an input/output (I/O) rule to automatically lock all doors at a specific time, such as the business's end time. This ensures that doors are secured even if they were manually unlocked earlier.
2. Stagger Locking Actions: To avoid conflicts, ensure that locking actions are staggered by a short interval, such as one minute. This prevents multiple doors from attempting to lock simultaneously, which could cause system errors.
Best Practices for Schedule Management
- Regularly review and update door schedules to align with operational needs.
- Train staff on the differences between manual and momentary unlocks to minimize disruptions to schedules.
- Use automated rules, such as I/O rules, to maintain schedule integrity and reduce manual interventions.
- Monitor system logs to identify and address any recurring issues with schedule compliance.
By understanding the impact of manual and momentary unlocks and implementing these best practices, you can ensure that your door schedules function smoothly and reliably.

title: Why can't I configure multi-day visits in Genea?
text:
## Why can't I configure multi-day visits in Genea?
Multi-day visit settings in Genea may sometimes be unavailable or restricted due to specific policies or user permissions. Below, we outline the common reasons for these restrictions and provide guidance on how to resolve them.
Overview of Multi-Day Visit Settings
Multi-day visit settings allow users to schedule visitor access for more than one day. However, these settings may be subject to restrictions based on building management policies or user roles within the Genea system.
Common Restrictions
1. Building Management Policies
Some buildings enforce restrictions on the duration of visitor access. For example, there may be a maximum limit, such as five days, for visitor access. If you need to schedule a visit longer than the allowed duration, you will need to contact your building management team for assistance.
2. User Role Permissions
Your ability to configure multi-day visits may also depend on your user role within the Genea system. For instance, if you are a user manager, you might not have the necessary permissions to add multi-day visits. In such cases, you should reach out to your onsite administrator for support.
Steps to Resolve Multi-Day Visit Issues
1. Check Building Policies: Verify if your building has any restrictions on the duration of visitor access. Contact your building management team for clarification or to request an exception.
2. Review User Permissions: Confirm your role and permissions within the Genea system. If you lack the necessary permissions, contact your onsite administrator to assist with configuring multi-day visits.
FAQs
Why is there a restriction on multi-day visits?
Restrictions are often implemented by building management to maintain security and control over visitor access.
Who should I contact if I encounter issues with multi-day visits?
- For policy-related restrictions, contact your building management team.
- For permission-related issues, contact your onsite administrator.
By understanding these restrictions and following the outlined steps, you can effectively address any issues related to multi-day visit settings in Genea.

title: Camera Wall Setup and Timeline View – Mobile App
description: This article walks you through how to set up your Camera Wall, manage cameras, and use the Timeline playback controls.
text:
The Camera Wall in the Genea Mobile Access app for Arcules VMS integration lets you view all your site cameras in one place, monitor live feeds, scrub through recorded footage using the Timeline View, and trigger a Quick Grant to unlock paired doors directly from the camera view.
___________________________________________________________
1. Access the Camera Wall
1. Open the Genea Mobile Access app and sign in.
2. Tap Control Center at the bottom navigation bar.
3. Tap the Camera Wall tab at the top of the screen.
If no cameras have been added yet, you will see the No Camera Yet placeholder screen with an Add camera to start message.
___________________________________________________________
2. Add Cameras to the Camera Wall
1. From the empty Camera Wall screen, tap Add in the top-right corner.
2. The Add Cameras sheet opens, listing all cameras available at your site under AVAILABLE CAMERAS (for example, Demo Unit 2386, Equipment Configuration Room, Kitchen Door).
3. Tap the circle next to each camera you want to add to your Camera Wall. A check mark indicates the camera is selected.
4. Tap Done in the top-right corner to save your selection.
5. Tap Cancel to exit without making changes.
___________________________________________________________
3. View Live Camera Feeds
Once cameras are added, they appear as live tiles on the Camera Wall.
- While a feed is loading, the tile displays a Buffering indicator in yellow.
- Once the stream is ready, a red Live badge appears in the lower-right corner of the tile, confirming the live feed is active.
- The camera name (for example, Kitchen Door) is displayed in the upper-left corner of each tile.
___________________________________________________________
4. Edit or Rearrange Cameras
To manage the cameras shown on your Camera Wall:
1. Tap the three-dot (⋯) menu in the top-right of the Cameras section header.
2. A pop-up appears with two options:
   - Edit – Add or remove cameras from the wall.
   - Rearrange – Reorder cameras to set the display priority on your wall.
3. Select the option you need and follow the prompts.
___________________________________________________________
5. Open a Camera in Full-Screen View
To inspect a camera feed more closely:
1. Tap any camera tile on the Camera Wall to open the full-screen view.
2. The camera name is shown at the top, and the live timestamp (date and time) appears in the upper-right corner.
3. Tap the back arrow (<) in the top-left to return to the Camera Wall.
4. Tap the expand icon in the top-right to switch to landscape (full-screen) mode.
In landscape mode, the camera feed fills the entire screen for a wider field of view. A Live badge in the lower-right confirms the stream is real-time.
___________________________________________________________
6. Use Quick Grant from the Camera View
If the camera is paired with a door (for example, the Kitchen Door), you can unlock the door directly from the live feed without leaving the camera screen.
1. In full-screen view, locate the lock icon with the >>>>>> swipe arrows at the bottom-center of the screen.
2. Swipe the lock icon to the right to trigger a Quick Grant.
3. Once the door unlocks, the lock icon turns green and the message "Quick grant was successful." appears on screen.
___________________________________________________________
7. Use the Timeline View for Recorded Playback
The Timeline View lets you scrub back through recorded footage to review past events.
Understanding the Timeline
At the bottom of the full-screen camera view, you will see a horizontal timeline with hour markers (for example, 9 AM, 10 AM, 11 AM, 12 PM):
- Orange bars indicate periods when recorded footage is available.
- White / blank bars indicate time periods with no recording.
- A blue marker with the current timestamp (for example, 10:13) shows your current playback position.
Scrubbing Through Footage
1. Drag the blue timestamp marker left or right along the timeline to jump to any point in the recording or click on the Date & Time to select specific date & time.
2. Release at the desired time, and the camera view updates to show footage from that moment.
3. The date (for example, 5/7/26) and the selected playback time (for example, 6:53 AM) are displayed on the left side of the screen.
Playback Controls
Tap the center of the screen during playback to display playback controls:
- Rewind 10 seconds – Tap the circular arrow with 10 on the left to jump back 10 seconds.
- Pause / Play – Tap the center button to pause or resume playback.
- Forward 10 seconds – Tap the circular arrow with 10 on the right to skip ahead 10 seconds.
Return to Live View
To exit playback and return to the real-time feed:
- Tap the Go Live button on the right side of the screen while in playback mode, or
- Tap the red Live badge to jump straight to the most recent live feed.

title: Bulk User Import via CSV in Building & Tenant Portal
text:
Genea’s new Bulk User Import via CSV feature makes it faster and easier to onboard and manage users at scale. Rather than creating users individually, you can now upload a CSV file directly through the Genea web platform to import or update multiple users in one step.
___________________________________________________________
Where to Find It
The Bulk User Import option is available in the “All Users” section under the “More” menu.
Note: This feature is available for:
- Building Portals
- Tenant Portals (Non-UG)
- Enterprise Portals (Non-UG)
___________________________________________________________
What You Can Do With It
- With the CSV upload tool, you can:
- Create new users
- Update existing users
- Assign access groups and building access groups
- Configure card credentials
- Assign PINs
- Assign elevator-related fields
- Map custom attributes
- Track imports using tags
- Handle up to 10,000 records in a single file
___________________________________________________________
Preparing Your CSV File
Click “Download Template” to get a sample CSV file format.
The standard supported fields include:
File Requirements
- File must be in .csv format.
- File size and number of users must not exceed system limits
  Limit: 10,000 records or 10MB (shown in upload dialog).
- Mandatory fields must be filled correctly, or the upload will fail with an error message
___________________________________________________________
## Uploading Your File
1. Go to All Users → More → Import Users
2. Click Upload File
3. Select your .csv file
4. The system validates:
   - File type
   - File size
   - Record count
   - CSV structure
5. Map CSV columns to Genea attributes
6. Configure update behavior
7. Review and start import
___________________________________________________________
## Mapping Attributes
After upload, the system automatically extracts CSV headers and allows administrators to map them to Genea attributes.
1. Mandatory Fields
The following field is required:
- Full Name
- Location
- Role
If mandatory fields are not mapped, the system displays a validation message before proceeding.
2. Unique Identifier
If you want to update existing users, select a Unique Identifier during mapping.
Only one unique identifier can be selected per import.
1. Supported Unique Identifiers
- UUID
- Email
- External ID
- Name + Tenant (Available in Building Portal only)
- Employee Number + Tenant (Available in Building Portal only)
2. Unique Identifier Behavior
- If Identifier Matches Existing User - The existing user is updated.
- If Identifier Does Not Exist - A new user is created.
- If No Identifier Is Selected - All records are treated as new users.
- If Identifier Value Is Blank - That specific row is treated as a new user.
- Duplicate Identifiers Within CSV - Duplicate row values are merged.
3. Multi-Column Mapping Support
The following attributes support mapping from multiple CSV columns:
- Access Groups
- Building Access Groups (BAGs)
Values from all selected columns are merged during processing.
4. Update Behaviour
During mapping, administrators can define how imported values should update existing users.
Supported Update Behavior:
- Override: Replaces existing values with imported values.
- Merge: Adds imported values while preserving existing assignments.
___________________________________________________________
## Import Tagging
Before starting the import:
- A default tag is automatically generated
- Administrators can edit the tag before proceeding
The tag is:
- Stored in import history
- Included in downloadable reports
- Available for filtering in the All Users page
Duplicate tags are not allowed for the same customer.
___________________________________________________________
## Import Progress
Once the import starts:
- Progress appears directly on the All Users page
- Administrators can monitor import status in real time
Only one import process is allowed per customer at any given time.
___________________________________________________________
## Import Summary
Once the import is completed, administrators can view a summary showing:
- Users Created
- Users Updated
- Users with Errors
- Unchanged Users
Administrators can also download a detailed CSV report containing:
- Row-level results
- Validation errors
- Failure reasons
Common Errors & Fixes
___________________________________________________________
Need Help?
If you experience any issues or have questions about your import, contact our support team at support@getgenea.com.​

title: Syncing Visitor Invitations in CRE Environments
description: Reverse Building Sync ensures that visitor invitations created in the Building Portal automatically appear in the relevant Tenant Portal — giving both teams full visibility into who's visiting, without any duplicate effort.
text:
Before you begin
To use Reverse Building Sync, make sure the following are in place:
1. The tenant must exist in the Building Portal and be linked (synced) to the building
2. The tenant location must have Visitor Management enabled
3. The Sync Building Invitation setting must be turned ON in the Tenant Portal & the visitor type used for syncing must be mapped correctly
How Reverse Building Sync works
When a Building admin creates a visitor invitation and selects a tenant:
1. The invite is created in the Building Portal
2. The system checks if the selected tenant is synced and has Visitor Management enabled
3. If yes, a matching invite is automatically created in the Tenant Portal
4. Both invites remain linked — updates to one are reflected in the other
Throughout the visitor lifecycle (invite creation, check-in, check-out, badge generation, card assignment), both portals stay aligned in real time.
Enabling Reverse Building Sync
Who can do this: Tenant admins
1. Navigate to Tenant Portal -> Location Settings
2. Locate the card titled "Sync Building Invitations"
3. Toggle Reverse Building Sync to ON
4. Map the correct Visitor Type to invitations syncing on the Tenant side
5. Save your changes
Once enabled, any visitor invite created at the Building level for your tenant will automatically sync into your Tenant Portal.
Pre-registered visitor check-in experience
When a visitor receives a pre-registration invitation from the Building Portal:
1. The visitor receives an invite email or SMS with a registration link
2. They open the link on their own device (phone, tablet, or laptop)
3. They are guided through a single, combined check-in flow that includes:
   - Default fields (name, email, mobile) — shown once even if both portals require them
   - Building questionnaires first, followed by Tenant questions next
   - Photo capture and NDA acceptance (if required by either portal)
4. The visitor completes check-in in one seamless flow — no duplicate questions
5. Once submitted, the visitor's status updates in both the Building and Tenant Portals
Managing synced invites:
Once an invite is synced, the following actions stay in sync across both portals:
Visitor Logs & Activity Logs
All visitor activity — check-ins, check-outs, badge events — is visible in both the Building and Tenant Portals for synced invites. It is also supported in the Global Overview -> Visitor Management Activity reports.
Physical card sync
When a building admin assigns a physical access card to a synced visitor:
1. The card assignment is created in the Building Portal
2. If card sync is enabled, the card automatically syncs to the Tenant Portal
3. The card's validity matches the invite's validity and updates if the invite is changed.
If card sync is turned off at the time of assignment, you'll see a prompt:
Card sync blocked This keycard cannot be synced from the Building Portal because the card sync setting is currently turned off. Contact your system administrator to enable this setting. Would you like to assign this keycard locally instead?
Choose Save to assign the card locally in the Tenant Portal, or Cancel to step out and enable card sync first.
Filtering and exporting visitor data
A new Invite Origin filter helps you distinguish between invites created at the building versus the tenant level.
1. Go to Visitor Logs or the Visitor Summary widget
2. Click Filters
3. Under Invite Origin, select one or both:
   - Building Created
   - Tenant Created
4. By default, no filter is applied — you'll see all invites

title: Assa Abloy DSR Version Upgrade Guide
description: This guide walks you through upgrading your Door Service Router (DSR) to a newer version.
text:
The upgrade preserves your existing database and configuration. As long as the DSR keeps its current IP address and settings, you will not need to reconfigure your locks.​
Please read the entire guide before you begin. Set aside a maintenance window, since the DSR and its related services will be temporarily unavailable during the upgrade.
___________________________________________________________
Before You Begin
Make sure you have the following ready:
- Login credentials for both the database and the DSR. You will need these during the upgrade.
- The DSR installer for the version you are upgrading to. Download it from the official download page provided by your Genea contact and save it to the machine (virtual machine) that runs the DSR.
- Your existing database password from the original installation. You will be prompted for it during the upgrade.
Stop the Genea Gateway services
Before starting the installer, stop the following two services on the Gateway machine:
- Genea Cloud-to-Gateway Service
- Genea Gateway-to-Cloud Service​
___________________________________________________________
Upgrade Steps
1. Download the required DSR version
Go to the official download page and locate the DSR version you want to install. Save the installer to the Gateway machine.
2. Start the upgrade
Right-click the downloaded .exe file and choose Run as administrator to launch the installer.​
A dialog box will appear showing the current version (for example, 8.0.18.0) and the expected version you are upgrading to (for example, 8.0.31.0).​
3. Verify the versions and proceed
Carefully confirm that the current and expected versions shown are correct. If they are, click Yes to continue with the installation.
4. Database configuration
During installation you will reach the Database Configuration step.
Important: Do not select the "Create New Database" checkbox. Leaving it unchecked ensures the upgrade uses your existing database and keeps all of your current data.
5. Complete the installation
From here, the process is similar to the original DSR installation.
- Database password prompt: When asked, provide your database password. We recommend using the same password that was set during the initial installation.
- If you are changing the database password: Be sure to update it in the Genea database script as well, so the two stay consistent.
The installer will then upgrade your DSR to the new version.
6. Restart the Gateway
Once the upgrade finishes, restart the Gateway machine (the virtual machine on which the DSR was upgraded).
7. Update the database backup script
Update your database backup script to reflect the new PostgreSQL version and its corresponding path changes.
8. Start the Genea service
After the backup script has been updated, start the Genea service to apply all changes.
___________________________________________________________
After the Upgrade
Your DSR is now running the new version. Because the IP address and settings were preserved, your locks should continue operating without any reconfiguration. Confirm that the Genea services are running and that your system is communicating normally.
If you run into any issues during or after the upgrade, contact Genea support for assistance.
